twoFactor.keyShape: Letters and the digits 2 to 7 only: a round character is always the letter O, never a zero, and there is no 1 to mistake for I or L. Spaces do not matter.
twoFactor.codesShape: Upper case, without the characters that look like each other: no O or zero, no I or one. Spaces and the dash are forgiven when you type one back in.

c1.title: Auth out of the box
c1.description: Google and GitHub OAuth with Better Auth. Sessions stored in your own database. No third-party auth service required.

c2.title: Stripe payments
c2.description: Subscription checkout, webhooks, and Customer Portal. Handles upgrades, downgrades, and cancellations automatically.

c3.description: Type-safe database layer with Prisma 7. Works with Neon, Supabase, Railway, or any PostgreSQL provider.

c5.description: Middleware-based auth guards. Public, auth, dashboard, and admin route groups with zero boilerplate per page.

c7.title: 1-click Vercel deploy
c7.description: Deploy button in the README. From clone to production in under an hour, plus a built-in demo mode to showcase your product, like this site's live demo.

c8.title: Plain Next.js, nothing to learn
c8.description: No compiler step, no config DSL, no proprietary CLI. The App Router, Server Actions and Prisma work as documented, so your Next.js knowledge transfers on day one, and every component stays swappable.

$kit.maintainerBody: . One person, working in the open: the roadmap says what is coming, the changelog says what already shipped, and every release is a tag you can read. Issues and questions are answered by the person who wrote the code.
$kit.noteBody: Tell your story here: what you are building, who it is for, and why it exists. Edit this page in <path>src/app/[locale]/(public)/about/page.tsx</path>.
$kit.what: A complete starting point for a SaaS, not a demo of one. Authentication with OAuth, magic links and passwords. Stripe subscriptions, one-time payments and webhooks whose signature is verified before anything reaches the database. An admin panel with real revenue figures, transactional email, a file-based blog and the marketing site around it. It is the plumbing every product needs and nobody enjoys writing twice, in a codebase small enough to read in an afternoon and yours to change.
$kit.who: People shipping on their own or in a small team, who would rather spend the weekend on the part that makes their product different than on wiring a checkout for the tenth time. It assumes you know Next.js, and that you would rather own the code than rent a platform.

items.question: Is there really no limit on how many documents I send?
items.answer: No plan has a cap. {site} doesn't count envelopes, and paid plans add features like Sign & Pay and sequential signing, never more sends. Fair-use limits apply to prevent spam.

items.question: Are electronic signatures legally binding?
items.answer: In most countries, yes, including under the US ESIGN Act, the EU's eIDAS regulation and Ghana's Electronic Transactions Act. Every signed PDF from {site} carries a certificate with a tamper-evident hash and a full audit trail of who signed, when and from where.

items.question: What if I sent it to the wrong email?
items.answer: Open the document, tap Edit next to the recipient and fix the address. The old link stops working immediately and the right person gets a new one. Nothing needs to be rebuilt.

items.question: How does Sign & Pay work?
items.answer: Connect Stripe or Paystack once, then set an amount on any document. The signer pays at the end of signing, by card or mobile money, and the money settles to your own account.

items.question: How do I cancel?
items.answer: One button on your billing page. You keep access until the end of the period you paid for, we email you before any renewal, and your documents stay exportable even after you cancel.

items.question: What exactly do I get?
items.answer: You get a production-ready Next.js 16 codebase with Better Auth, Stripe, Prisma, and Tailwind pre-configured. Clone the repo, set your env variables, and deploy. Everything works out of the box.

items.question: Why not ShipFast or Makerkit?
items.answer: {site} uses a best-of-breed stack where every component is independent. No Supabase lock-in, no proprietary auth layer. If a dependency releases a breaking change, you update one package, not the entire stack.

items.question: Which database providers are supported?
items.answer: Any PostgreSQL provider: Neon (recommended, cheapest), Supabase, Railway, PlanetScale (via Postgres mode), or self-hosted. Just set your DATABASE_URL and run the migration.

items.question: Do I need a Stripe account?
items.answer: Yes. Stripe is used for subscription payments. You'll need to create products and prices in your Stripe dashboard and add the price IDs to your env vars. The setup guide covers this step by step.

items.question: Can I use this for client projects?
items.answer: Yes, MIT license. Use it for as many projects as you want, including client work. No per-project fees.

items.question: What if I need help or find a bug?
items.answer: Open an issue on GitHub. It's open source, so you get every update and bug fix by pulling the latest main. For direct support, reach out via email.

setup.subtitle: The app is running. It needs a database before it can show anything else.
setup.step1Body: First create a PostgreSQL database (Neon has a free tier). Then copy .env.example to .env.local next to this project: .env.local is the file you edit, the example stays as it is. Put the connection string in DATABASE_URL, and fill AUTH_SECRET with what this command prints.
setup.step1Note: Every time you change .env.local, stop the dev server (Ctrl+C) and start it again: the values are read when it boots.
setup.step1Unreachable: DATABASE_URL is set, but the database did not answer. Check the connection string in .env.local: the host, the password, and that the database still exists.
setup.step2Body: The first creates the tables, the second adds the example plans.
setup.step2Note: Seeing an SSL warning in the terminal? The string Neon gives you ends with sslmode=require: change it to sslmode=verify-full in .env.local.
setup.step3Body: Stop the dev server and start it again. The landing page comes back, and Sign in has a Dev Login (Admin) button that needs no OAuth app.

detail.cancelBody: Signing links stop working. Anything already signed stays in the audit trail and your export.

detail.filesHint: Download any time, on any plan, even after cancelling.
